title: CSS @property: typed and registered custom properties
learningObjectives: Explain css @property: typed and registered custom properties and its role in modern CSS.
Write valid CSS syntax and predict the computed result.
Choose the technique appropriate to a real interface requirement.
Identify common implementation, accessibility, and browser-support pitfalls.
Test and explain the behaviour using browser developer tools.

understand.concept: The @property at-rule registers a CSS custom property with a declared syntax, inheritance behaviour, and initial value. Its descriptors include syntax, inherits, and initial-value. Registration allows the browser to parse and validate values according to the declared syntax and can make custom properties interpolate during transitions when the registered type supports animation. Unregistered custom properties are token streams and do not interpolate as typed values in the same way. The syntax descriptor is a string such as '<color>' or '<length>'; universal syntax '*' accepts arbitrary token sequences. Check browser support and provide a useful fallback.
understand.whyItMatters: Registered custom properties make design tokens more predictable and can enable smooth transitions for values such as colours and lengths. They also introduce a new layer of CSS behaviour that developers must understand before relying on it.
understand.analogy: An @property registration is like declaring the data type and default value of a variable before using it.
understand.analogyLimit: CSS custom properties are not JavaScript variables; their cascade, inheritance, parsing, and computed-value rules are specific to CSS.

explain.narrative: Register a colour token and animate it between two values. Then remove the registration and compare how the browser interpolates the custom property.

examples.explanation: The custom property is registered as a colour, inherits, and has an initial value. The browser can interpolate the registered colour during the transition in supporting browsers.
examples.expectedOutput: A button background smoothly changes from blue to pink on hover in supporting browsers.

examples.explanation: The length syntax constrains the value and the property does not inherit. The grid gap can animate as a typed length when supported.
examples.expectedOutput: The grid gap grows from 1rem to 2rem on hover in supporting browsers.

practise.guidedTask: Register a colour and a length custom property with explicit syntax, inheritance, and initial values. Animate each and inspect computed styles in a supporting browser.
practise.independentTask: Design a token system that uses registered custom properties where useful and ordinary custom properties elsewhere. Include a fallback for browsers that do not support the required registration behaviour.
hints: Declare syntax, inherits, and initial-value in the @property block.
The syntax descriptor is a quoted CSS syntax string.
Do not assume every browser version supports every @property behaviour; test and provide fallbacks.

questions.prompt: Which at-rule registers a typed CSS custom property?
questions.explanation: The @property at-rule defines a custom property's syntax and inheritance behaviour.

questions.prompt: Which descriptors are required in a basic @property registration?
questions.explanation: A registration declares the accepted syntax, inheritance behaviour, and initial value.

options: The custom property accepts CSS color values
The property is a font family
The value is always a number
questions.answer: The custom property accepts CSS color values
questions.explanation: The syntax descriptor constrains the registered value type.

questions.prompt: Why can a registered custom property animate more predictably?
options: The browser knows its value type and can interpolate compatible values
questions.answer: The browser knows its value type and can interpolate compatible values
questions.explanation: Typed registration gives the browser information needed for type-aware interpolation.

questions.prompt: What should production code do about browser support?
options: Test support and provide a sensible fallback
Assume every browser supports every feature
questions.answer: Test support and provide a sensible fallback
questions.explanation: Feature support varies, so test the target environment and design a fallback.
